assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clear discovery in nature: the baryon acoustic peak provides a standard ruler that has become a cornerstone measurement of the expansion history and of dark energy. It is original, cleanly interpretable and has lasting impact on the questions about the accelerating universe that matter most to cosmology and fundamental theory.
assessment.attribution: The 2005 detections came from the SDSS luminous red galaxy sample (Eisenstein and collaborators) and the 2dFGRS power spectrum (Cole and the 2dFGRS team). Peacock led much of the 2dFGRS analysis, but his role as a decisive contributor is less sharp than the other two; the theoretical prediction side (Peebles, Yu, Sunyaev, Zeldovich) is outside the supplied names, which complicates a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mature: two independent surveys in 2005, followed by BOSS, eBOSS and DESI, with consistent results across many redshifts. The interpretation is stable. Recent DESI hints of evolving dark energy are a reason for interest, not a doubt about the BAO measurement itself.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views BAO as a discovery distinct from earlier CMB and supernova prizes.
Division of credit between the two 2005 detections and between large collaborations and named individuals; I am working from memory and have not verified roles.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened an entire field: a theoretical prediction (quantum spin Hall and Z2 topology) confirmed by experiment in HgTe and then in 3D materials, with a broad conceptual impact on band theory and quantum matter. It is a case where the idea was checked against nature.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive 2005 theoretical proposal, and Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (not in the supplied names) predicted the HgTe case. Molenkamp's group did the 2007 experimental observation, and Hasan did the first 3D topological insulator work. Choosing three from the four supplied names forces dropping Mele, which is awkward given the Kane-Mele pairing.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with roughly two decades of independent confirmation across many material platforms and ARPES and transport probes. Timing is good given the 2016 prize for topological phase transitions.
uncertainties: Attribution is contested because of the omitted Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Fu-Kane-Mele contributions and the unavoidable cut to three.
Overlap with the 2016 prize may make the committee cautious about novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A theory prediction of flat bands at a magic angle followed by a striking experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene. It is a clear example of theory guided by and confirmed by experiment, and it created the whole field of moire quantum materials.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 continuum-model prediction, and Jarillo-Herrero's group (with Yuan Cao as first author) made the 2018 experimental discovery. The three supplied names form a sensible theory-plus-experiment configuration, although other contributors (for example Santos and Peres, Lopes dos Santos, Kim) may have claims I cannot assess.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing, with many independent replications since 2018. The nature of the superconducting pairing is still debated, which suggests the field may still be young for a prize.
uncertainties: The origin of superconductivity and the correlated phases is unresolved.
Prize may be premature compared with more settled fields; priority questions about earlier theory papers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first direct images of the shadow of a black hole (M87* in 2019, Sgr A* in 2022) are a visual confirmation of strong-field gravity and of the horizon-scale picture, with an existential appeal. This is the kind of clue from nature the committee likes, although it is a measurement against a well-established prediction.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging idea, Doeleman led the VLBI development and the collaboration, and Moran led the early mm-VLBI technique. The EHT is a large collaboration of several hundred people, so any three-person configuration risks being seen as arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Results are confirmed for two sources with consistent shadow sizes, but the precision is limited and tests of alternatives to the Kerr black hole remain modest. Recognition may be somewhat early, though the 2020 prize already recognized black-hole theory and the Galactic centre.
uncertainties: Large-collaboration credit and whether three people can fairly represent the achievement.
Whether the imaging constrains deviations from general relativity enough to count as a lasting scientific discovery rather than a technical achievement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the identification of the first sources (TXS 0506+056 blazar, NGC 1068) opened neutrino astronomy as a new window on the universe. It is a clear observational discovery with lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube, and Karle was a leading figure in construction and analysis. The result belongs to a large collaboration, so a prize to two individuals leaves other founders (for example the AMANDA and DUMAND pioneers) unrecognised, and I cannot verify their relative roles.
assessment.maturity: The 2013 diffuse flux is well established and independently supported by the Antarctic and Mediterranean detectors. Source identification is more recent, with a small number of sources at modest significance, so some interpretations are still developing.
uncertainties: Source associations (blazar versus Seyfert) rest on few objects.
Fair credit among IceCube founders and the earlier Cherenkov neutrino-telescope pioneers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP's precision CMB maps turned cosmology into a precision science and fixed the parameters of the Lambda-CDM model, including strong evidence for dark energy and a nearly flat universe. The impact is large, although the 2006 prize for COBE and the later Planck results reduce the novelty.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page was a key instrument and experimental figure, and Spergel was a leading analysis and interpretation figure. The mission was a large collaboration with many essential contributors, so the configuration is defensible but not unique.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with Planck and ground-based experiments confirming and surpassing the results. Because Planck superseded it, the committee might see recognition of WMAP as late or as overlapping with earlier CMB prizes.
uncertainties: Overlap with the COBE prize of 2006 and the 2019 cosmology prize.
Whether the committee prefers to honour a mission, a technique, or the cosmological parameters.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, have reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and make possible tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and searches for ultralight dark matter. It is a precise measurement tool with a plausible link to fundamental physics.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and made the first demonstrations, and Ye's group pushed the stability and accuracy records. The two names form a compact configuration, though earlier work on optical frequency combs (prize 2005) and ion clocks (Wineland, 2012) overlaps conceptually.
assessment.maturity: Mature in performance and independently reproduced by many laboratories, but the redefinition of the second is still pending and the fundamental-physics payoff is so far upper limits rather than discoveries.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes on frequency combs and ion clocks.
Whether fundamental-physics results will emerge to strengthen the case.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The realisation of strongly interacting Fermi gases (Feshbach resonances, the BEC-BCS crossover, superfluidity and universal thermodynamics) provides a clean laboratory for strongly correlated fermion physics, with connections to neutron stars and the quark-gluon plasma. It is original and conceptually important, although it follows the 2001 BEC prize.
assessment.attribution: Grimm, Ketterle and Salomon each reached the molecular BEC and the crossover, with Jin (deceased) and Thomas, Zwierlein and others also contributing. Ketterle is already a laureate, which might weigh against him. The three names are credible but the allocation is not unambiguous.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with two decades of replication, though the main discoveries date from 2003-2005, so recognition is late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Credit among Grimm, Ketterle, Salomon, Thomas, Zwierlein and the late Deborah Jin.
Whether a second prize to a prior laureate is acceptable to the committee.
